source_refs.note: Topic 5.4.1.1 Model Development with the improvement tip (PDF 135-136, printed 132-133). Long question 2 is answered.

items: Define the problem: understand it and the factors that affect it, such as family size, location or income for grocery spending.
Collect data: past spending, number of family members and other relevant factors.
Choose an algorithm: a method for creating the model, such as linear or logistic regression.
Train the model: let it learn from the data to make predictions.
Evaluate the model: test it on new data to see how well it predicts.

blocks.text: To improve a model: use more data points, include relevant factors such as family size or special events, update it regularly with new data, and test predictions against actual spending (Tip).

blocks.alt: Top left: five points of customers against earnings on the line earnings = 100 + 40 x customers, with a prediction of Rs 980 for 22 customers and an actual day-6 point of 1,250. Top right: an S-shaped probability curve over pass/fail points for 1 to 6 hours of study. Bottom left: Math and English scores of five students in two K-means clusters with centres marked x. Bottom right: five model-building steps.
blocks.caption: Linear regression, logistic regression and K-means (original diagram after topic 5.4).
blocks.long_description: The fruit-stall data lie exactly on the line earnings = 100 + 40 x customers, so 22 customers predict 980 rupees, and on day 6 the model predicted 1,220 for 28 customers against an actual 1,250. A logistic model turns study hours into a probability of passing that rises in an S-shape from near 0 to near 1, crossing 0.5 between the failing and passing students; the curve drawn is illustrative. K-means with K = 2 groups Basim, Umer and Maliha around a centre at Math 78.3, English 65, and Anie and Tallat around Math 45, English 82.5. A model is built by defining the problem, collecting data, choosing an algorithm, training and evaluating on new data.

blocks.prompt: Describe the steps in building a basic statistical model such as linear regression, including data collection, training and evaluation (long question 2).
blocks.explanation: Define the question and the variables (for the fruit stall: customers as X, earnings as Y). Collect reliable data, clean it and plot it to check the relationship looks straight. Choose linear regression and train it: find the slope and intercept that fit the data (here earnings = 100 + 40 x customers). Evaluate it on new data by comparing predictions with actual values (28 customers: predicted 1,220, actual 1,250, error 30) and use error or accuracy metrics; then interpret the result and update the model as new data arrive.

items: Five steps: define the problem, collect data, choose an algorithm, train, evaluate on new data.
